title: Household Usage Fee Cap — Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program Billing Rule
content:
**Billing rule.** Under the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program, usage fees net of meal-status waivers are capped per household per school year at the maximum usage fees per household per school year after waivers. The excess of a new usage fee over the remaining cap room is credited as a household cap credit. Summer checkouts belong to the school year that just ended, and late, cleaning, repair and replacement charges never count toward the cap.

## Quantities the rule uses

1. **The school year.** The cap is counted within the school year of the usage fee being charged. A Summer Instrument Checkout belongs to the school year that just ended, so its usage fee counts within that school year.
2. **Usage fees already counted.** For a new usage fee, the household's usage fees already counted are the usage fees posted earlier on the household's other checkouts of that school year, less the free meal waiver, reduced meal waiver and household cap credits posted against those fees.
3. **Remaining cap room.** The remaining cap room is the cap less the usage fees already counted.
4. **The household cap credit.** The new usage fee, net of its own meal-status waiver, is added to the usage fees already counted; the amount by which that total exceeds the cap is credited against the new usage fee as a household cap credit. When the total does not exceed the cap, no household cap credit is posted.

Only usage fees enter the count. A late return fee, a fee for an uncleaned return, a repair charge and a replacement charge are never counted toward the cap.

## Worked example on hypothetical figures

The cap figure below is hypothetical, chosen only to show the arithmetic; the real cap is the figure the program's rate table states.

Hypothetical cap: 150.00. The household's checkouts of one school year post usage fees in this order:

| Order posted | Usage fee | Meal-status waiver | Usage fees already counted before it | Total with the new fee net of waiver | Household cap credit | Net counted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First checkout | 90.00 | none | 0.00 | 90.00 | 0.00 | 90.00 |
| Second checkout | 90.00 | none | 90.00 | 180.00 | 30.00 | 60.00 |
| Third checkout | 40.00 | half waived, 20.00 | 150.00 | 170.00 | 20.00 | 0.00 |

The second fee brings the total 30.00 above the cap, so 30.00 is credited; the third fee's net amount of 20.00 falls entirely above the cap and is credited in full.

## Points of judgement

- **A late fee on the same checkout.** A late return fee posted after the cap is reached is charged in full; it never counts toward the cap.
- **A summer checkout after the spring term.** The usage fee of a Summer Instrument Checkout is counted with the usage fees of the school year that just ended.
- **A different school year.** Usage fees of an earlier school year are not usage fees already counted for a fee charged in the next school year.
